questions.question: 1. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a regular LDPC code with a $5$-by-$6$ parity-check matrix $H$ of rank $3$. Select the correct pair for the $\textbf{ rate }$ and $\textbf{ design rate }$ of the code.

explanations.a: Incorrect. The code rate is correct, but the design rate should be calculated by $\frac{\text{ number of rows of } H}{\text{ number of columns of } H}$.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The design rate is correct, but the code rate is incorrect. The code rate is calculated by $\frac{\text{ rank of }H}{n}$
explanations.c: Incorrect. Both the rate and design rate are incorrect. The rate is calculate by $\frac{\text{ rank of } H}{n}$, and the design rate should be calculated by $\frac{\text{ number of rows of } H}{\text{ number of columns of } H}$.
explanations.d: Correct. The code rate is $\frac{\text{ rank of }H}{n}$, and the design rate is calculate by $\frac{\text{ number of rows of } H}{\text{ number of columns of } H}$.

questions.question: 3. Which of the following is a characteristic property of a bipartite graph?

answers.a: It contains at least one odd cycle.
answers.b: All vertices can be divided into two sets such that no two vertices within the same set are adjacent.
answers.c: All edges of the graph connect vertices within the same set.
answers.d: It contains an even number of vertices.

explanations.a: Incorrect. A bipartite graph cannot have odd cycles.
explanations.b: Correct. This is the defining characteristic of a bipartite graph.
explanations.c: Incorrect. This is not true; edges in bipartite graphs connect vertices from different sets.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The number of vertices is not necessarily even in bipartite graphs.

questions.question: 4. Which of the following LDPC codes is expected to perform better in practice, particularly in terms of error correction capability, given sufficient large block length?

answers.a: A regular LDPC code with large block lengths.
answers.b: An irregular LDPC code with large block lengths.
answers.c: A regular LDPC code with short block lengths.
answers.d: An irregular LDPC code with short block lengths.

explanations.a: Incorrect. While regular LDPC codes are easier to analyze, they may not perform as well as irregular codes in practice with large block lengths due to optimized connections.
explanations.b: Correct. Irregular LDPC codes are known to perform better in practice, wspecially with large block lengths, as their structureallows for optimized variable and check node connections.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Short block lengths reduce error correction performance in both regular and irregular codes.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Irregular LDPC codes perform better with larger block lengths, so short block lengths reduce performance.
